coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K09 (free state 'Gens de maison' platform). Not searched again.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Export of scrap and ferrous by-products banned by ministerial decree of 23 June 2023 (Global Trade Alert); collection by ferrailleurs stays legal (govt spokesman, 21 July 2023). No dealer licence, register or reporting duty found. Currency of the ban in Oct 2026 unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No dedicated search (budget spent on higher-yield categories). No Benin rule seen incidentally.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: One search returned only Ivory Coast, Mali and French texts. No Benin gold-buyer register or comptoir rule found. Mining-code and DGM rules unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or casse licence found. A vehicle-fleet renewal programme mentions a planned end-of-life-vehicle recycling channel, but no adopted text. Customs circular of 6 May 2022 defines 'new' vehicle as at most 12 months and 6,000 km. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K12. Decree 88-258 (1988) on professions linked to livestock and meat trade is listed by the agriculture ministry; its current status is unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Only academic studies and a ministry compilation of old texts (law 84-009, decree 88-258, ordinance 72-31). No butcher licensing or carte sanitaire found. ABSSA is the food-safety body.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: EU listed Benin for honey on 15 Feb 2018. Cooperatives exist (560 beekeepers per World Bank). No individual beekeeper register or recurring duty found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Decree 2014-352 (veterinary medicines regime) and a 2018 order allow para-professionals to open practices and pharmacies. Only 44 authorisations were issued in 2019. Tiny buyer group, no register found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: DGEau publishes a 45-page guide on authorisation/declaration procedures; the water code is law 2010-44. No abstraction fee or driller register found. Contents of the guide not read.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: 11 Jan 2024: 12 of 20 applicant desludging firms received state approval. A body called SGDS is to monitor and control sludge collection and transport. Very small closed buyer group.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Benin text on lifts, boilers or pressure equipment found. Decree 2021-226 regulates technical-control approval in general. Apave Benin offers pressure inspection (ISO 9001 certificate). Dominant incumbent, no owner-side duty found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Village water systems (AEV) are run under lease by private operators; the operator files a monthly activity and financial report to the town hall by the 5th. ANAEP-MR (created 2017) publishes semi-annual performance reports and uses the mWater platform. Current operators and regional lease status unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Decree 2018-172 requires pesticide registration or provisional sales authorisation; decree 2018-171 creates the CNGP. No distributor or fertiliser-dealer approval text or register found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: New order n°009/MTFP/DC/SGM/DGT/DRPDS/SMO/SA of 11 April 2025 (under law 2017-05) sets approval conditions for placement agencies; ministry publishes an application form. Reporting duties and transition deadline not found. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Decree 2024-991 of 19 June 2024 replaces the 1995 order: categories, technical and sanitary norms, minimum qualifications and sanctions for funeral firms, funeral homes, crematoria and cemeteries; morgue storage max one month. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Law 2025-19 (July 2025) and decree 2025-575 (24 Sep 2025) created an online registry live from 19 Dec 2025, covering all associations, religious and mutual bodies, NGOs and foundations. Compliance extended three months by communiqué of 4 May 2026. Further decrees adopted 8 Oct 2025. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: ANaTT SYGFR freight platform: mandatory registration of carriers, trucks, drivers, forwarders (XOF 3,000/yr national). Electronic waybill pilot from 24 Sep 2025. Tokpa-tokpa minibus strike from 13 July 2026 over technical-inspection refusals for modified vehicles. Moto-taxi is K11. Candidates C5, C6.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: BCEAO/Finance instruction 07-07-2025/RFE on manual exchange, in force 1 Aug 2025: natural persons must re-apply as legal entities within one year; entities lacking financial resources have one year. Regulator flagged poor registers and over-threshold sales. Dantokpa market relocated from Jan 2026. Candidates C2, C9.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools are K03. The nursery search returned only French results; no Benin childcare licensing text found. Tattoo, food producers and hunting outfitters not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Decree 2023-423 (26 Jul 2023): approval to import/store/distribute refined products, issued online by the commerce minister after a technical commission. Old approval decrees required quarterly stock declarations and a one-month reserve stock (old, nominative, may not apply now). ANM ran surprise checks on stations in 2024 and sealed some stations in Abomey-Calavi for non-compliant pumps. Only generic foreign station software found (Stationnex, Station Manager). Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Thin. Soy export is free but only through Cotonou port, and a raw-soy export ban from 1 Apr 2024 was reported (current status unconfirmed). Cashew is covered by K05. No trader or warehouse register found. Nothing new beyond K05.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Microfinance (SFD) is governed by law 2025-14 (July 2025, per the e-Contrôle article); SFDs file periodic and annual data to ANSSFD via the e-Contrôle platform, and a new mandatory IDENTIFIANT sheet was added (article dated 8 Sep 2026). About 30 approved mutualist SFDs are not in a network (2019 data). Agricultural co-operatives register under the OHADA co-operatives uniform act via the departmental agriculture directorates; no recurring filing found. Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Law 2025-01 on private practice (adopted Jan 2025, second reading Jun 2026, per press): Order-registered professionals no longer need prior authorisation, and non-professional investors may fund private health establishments except practices. ARCH insurance is run by ANPS; no public procedure found for private providers billing it. Candidate C04 (unverified).

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Regulator is ABMed (formerly ABRP). Drug and precursor control is under law 97-025. A 2016 order sets declaration and destruction of pharmaceutical waste for wholesalers. No precursor-user filing found. Candidate C09 (unverified).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No Benin private-security or cleaning-agency licensing text found. Press describes security guards working without contracts. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining code law 2006-17 requires a quarry opening and exploitation authorisation. Since the Council of Ministers of 9 Dec 2020, communes may issue them, and unauthorised quarries were ordered closed. Holders must issue a loading slip (bon de chargement) to each buyer and pay local development tax (TDL) and mining royalties. No contractor accreditation or local-content rule found. Candidate C06.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Only the CENTIF decree 2006-752 and the old UEMOA uniform law 2006-14 surfaced. The current Benin AML law, the DNFBP list, and any register of beneficial owners could not be confirmed. Candidate C10 (unverified).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Only a departmental measure found (Zou prefect: daily ID-based guest registration, register shown each morning at the police station). No national tourism-levy or short-term-rental declaration found. Candidate C08.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Customs brokers (commissionnaires en douane) are licensed under decree 99-563 and there is an authorised-economic-operator (AEO) programme from 2019. Phytosanitary rules rest on law 91-004. Cashew and soy are covered by K05. No new traceability duty found. Candidate C07 (unverified).

coverage.category: 31. Party halls (salles de fête): opening and operating authorisation and noise rules
coverage.found: Council of Ministers decree of 29 Nov 2023: authorisation required to open and run party halls, with parking sized to capacity and hygiene compliance. Existing halls had 12 months to comply. Tarpaulin halls are banned (noise decree 2022-301). Unannounced inspections and closures followed. Candidate C01.

coverage.category: 32. Legal metrology: scales, fuel pumps and other measuring instruments used in trade
coverage.found: Decree 86-216 (arts 8 and 12) requires initial verification and then periodic verification by ANM. Per La Nouvelle Tribune (Apr 2025), a compliant instrument gets a green sticker valid one year, and re-verification is annual. Seizures of uncertified scales at Cotonou fishing port (Jan 2025), market checks at Dantokpa (Aug 2025), and bakery bread-weight checks announced. Candidate C02.

coverage.category: 33. Bakeries: bread weight and price order
coverage.found: Order 0052 of 2008 fixes bread weights and prices. ANM announced bakery checks. No filing duty, only inspection. Candidate C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 34. Classified establishments and environmental audits (ABE)
coverage.found: Framework law 98-030; decree 2005-466 sets environmental audits (internal and external). An ABE-linked study reports 95 percent of audited units (2020-2023) had non-conformities. The national list of classified installations and any SME threshold were not found. Candidate C12 (unverified).

coverage.category: 35. Customs brokers and approved economic operators
coverage.found: Licensed under decree 99-563; about 30 brokers were summoned in 2021 (BEF). AEO programme since May 2019. The state guichet unique (GUCE) exists. Merged into candidate C07.

coverage.category: 36. Public registers for new companies and beneficial owners (monentreprise.bj, RCCM)
coverage.found: APIEX runs monentreprise.bj for online creation and formalisation. Benin is reported among six states with a beneficial-owner law, but Benin's own text and deadlines were not found. Covered under C10.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Benin-specific police register or licensing regime for general second-hand dealers or pawnbrokers surfaced in 7 French-language searches (all results for the French regime, not Benin). General trade law is loi 90-005 (as amended 1993): RCCM registration, carte professionnelle de commerçant, CCI membership. No pawnshop or mont-de-piete rule found; lending is under UEMOA/BCEAO microfinance rules and loi 2012-14 (regional framework, not a pawn rule). Only second-hand-specific Benin texts found are about used vehicles and motorbikes: decret 2004-708 (import of used mopeds/motorbikes, clearance needs production-year and anti-pollution test papers), decret 2004-236 (commission to census used-vehicle importers and owners/lessees of sales parks), decret 2000-671 art. 11 (age limit 10 years cars, 13 years utility vehicles, per a 2006 thesis, may be outdated) and the Ekpe park (2003, managers approved against a XOF 25M deposit, 31 plus 37 approved by 2004 per a 2008 study; night-circulation limits). Used clothing (Missebo market) and used phones: no Benin import ban, licence or IMEI-reseller rule found. Loi 2025-02 on competition (Jan 2025) found but no second-hand rule. Two sgg.gouv.bj decree PDFs were scanned images and could not be read. Net: nothing strong for a software product in this category; the used-vehicle park angle overlaps with category 5 and K03 is a different buyer.

result.competitor: For the filing itself, the free state portal service-public.bj and the electronic register. The ministry also gave free technical help during the extension. I found no Beninese association or NGO compliance software, and no published done-for-you offer. Lawyers and notaries likely do this work informally (not verified).
result.duty: Law 2025-19 (promulgated July 2025; gouv.bj dates it 25 July, most press 22 July) and Decree 2025-575 of 24 Sept 2025 create an electronic Register of Associations and Foundations. The Interior Ministry says it took effect on 19 Dec 2025 as the only way to declare, register and track associations, foundations and NGOs, with filing online via service-public.bj. Existing bodies had to bring their statutes into line within 9 months: 4 Aug 2025 to 3 May 2026, with automatic dissolution reported as the penalty. Communiqué 013-2026 of 4 May 2026 added 3 months. No source gives the exact end date, but by my count it is about early Aug 2026, so it has already passed (today is 9 Oct 2026). I found no further extension. On recurring duties, associations must keep proper accounts and produce annual reports, and the register receives activity reports and declarations of resources. I found no deadline, required format, auditor rule or penalty for these annual filings. An arrêté of 7 May 2026 sets fees of 50,000 FCFA for the declaration and 40,000 FCFA for publication in the register journal.
result.market: I found no current count. The latest figure is 12,022 civil-society organisations from the 2012-2013 RENOSC census (mentioned in search results; source not opened). Churches and mosques set up as associations would add to this. No register statistics have been published since Dec 2025.
result.reason: The duty is real, but the one-time rush to comply (re-registration) is very likely over, since the 3-month extension ended around Aug 2026. What remains is an annual activity report and resource declaration, for which I found no deadline, format or penalty. Filing is free on a state portal, and the ministry gave free help. Most buyers are small associations, churches and community groups with little budget, so willingness to pay is low. No software competitor exists, but the opening is small: at best a cheap done-for-you volume service, or bookkeeping and reporting templates for NGOs. Distribution through church federations is plausible. It could be confirmed if the decree's annual reporting deadline and penalties turn out to be strict.

result.competitor: I found no specific product for e-Contrôle template filling in Benin. ANSSFD itself provides the protected Excel templates and helps users at no cost. General IMF core-banking suites sold in the UMOA region (SBS SBP Core Amplitude, CapitalBanker MFI, Octopus, the older Aquadev ADbanking) produce regulatory reports, but I did not confirm whether they support Benin's e-Contrôle format. I did not identify which vendors small Beninese SFDs actually use.
result.duty: Approved SFDs/IMFs in Benin must send periodic and annual statistical and financial data to ANSSFD through the e-Contrôle platform. Per the article, the BCEAO regulation sets the frequency by institution category. A similar rule in Côte d'Ivoire uses monthly filing for article-44 SFDs and quarterly filing for the rest, within 30 days; Benin's exact split was not confirmed. Since September 2026 the AUTRES INDICATEURS file must include an IDENTIFIANT sheet, and files without it cannot be loaded. No penalties were found in sources. Law 2025-14 (microfinance, promulgated 2 July 2025 per press) is in force per press reports, but I did not see the text. ANSSFD is set up by Decree 2015-346.
result.market: BCEAO indicators count 53 SFDs in total for Benin at both 31 Mar 2025 and 30 Sep 2025 (22 of them in its monitored sample). The Ministry of Finance published a list of authorised SFDs dated 22 Apr 2024, but I did not count it. The claim's figure of about 30 unaffiliated mutuals comes from the 2019 directory and was not rechecked. The addressable market is a few dozen institutions at most.
result.reason: The duty is real. Beninwebtv (8 Sep 2026) says SFDs file periodic and annual data on ANSSFD's e-Contrôle platform. The AUTRES INDICATEURS file now has a mandatory IDENTIFIANT sheet, and a file missing it will not load. Law 2025-14 (adopted June 2025, promulgated 2 July 2025, per press) turns SFDs into IMFs. I did not see the law text, a penalty schedule or ANSSFD's own frequency rules. I found no vendor that does this job specifically for small Beninese SFDs. However, ANSSFD supplies protected Excel templates and offers free help, and UMOA core-banking packages (SBS, Capital Banking) target IMF reporting. The market is tiny: BCEAO counts 53 SFDs in Benin in total. Low volume, low willingness to pay and a free template mean a weak business.

The duty is real. BCEAO Instruction 07-07-2025/RFE (in force 1 Aug 2025) requires individual exchange agents to re-apply as legal entities within one year or lose their licence. The licensing and retention duty is real, but my search summaries did not cover the exact register and report formats. Benin Instruction 15/07/2025/RFE sets periodic reports to the Treasury and BCEAO. A BCEAO annual inspection flagged poor registers and missing reports. I found no dedicated software, but I ran only 2 searches and did not look for a competitor in depth. The market is probably only tens of agents, which is tiny. The re-licensing deadline of about Aug 2026 has already passed, so the one-off urgency is gone. Low volume and weak willingness to pay keep the score low.

The duty is real. Arrêté n°009/MTFP/DC/SGM/DGT/DRPDS/SMO/SA of 11 April 2025, under loi 2017-05, requires approval for any person or firm doing placement or recruitment intermediation. Sanctions run up to withdrawal of approval. The ministry's application form lists a large file, including a bank guarantee fund, CNSS registration and a criminal record extract. I found no placement-specific software or e-platform, but my searches were thin. Weak points: the sources say nothing on registers, periodic reports, renewal period or transition deadline, so recurrence is unproven. The market is probably a few hundred agencies at most (no register count found). The approval file is one-off, with little to sell on repeat. Willingness to pay is low.

The duty exists but is only partly verified. The Council of Ministers of 19 June 2024 adopted a decree on funeral services, funeral homes, crematoriums and cemeteries. It sets technical, sanitary and environmental norms, minimum qualifications and penalties. It also limits morgue storage to one month, with burial within 30 days. I did not read the decree text. I could not confirm the number 2024-991, the approval procedure, any register or filing duty, a transition deadline, or who inspects. No Benin-specific competitor turned up. Only generic foreign funeral software exists (Funetec, CemeteryPro). A 2018 thesis says existing cemetery software misses Benin needs. The buyer base is small and informal, with weak enforcement and low willingness to pay, and no recurring filing is confirmed. The score stays low.

The duty is real. SYGFR, run by ANaTT, requires transporters, trucks (transport cards), drivers and customs agents to register. Cards cost 3,000 FCFA/yr nationally and 1,000 FCFA per country internationally. Trailer conformity costs 12,000 FCFA. The e-waybill (LVE) launched 18 Mar 2025, and an international LVE pilot began 24 Sep 2025. Nothing I opened gave a penalty, a deadline or a statute; the "mandatory" claim comes from secondary summaries. SYGFR is a free state portal that already does the core job, including fleet/vehicle listing and authorizations (the Enabel transporter guide). That makes a third-party filing tool redundant. Only about 1,300 transporters are enrolled, so the market is small and fees are low. No private competitor was found, but that came from one search. The only gap is a renewal-reminder add-on, which is thin. Penalty, SYGFR API and fleet size were not checked.
